answer: Agents stake a bond tied to a unique hardware-rooted identity, and each epoch a random quorum audits a sample of peers. A sybil must fund many independent bonds, then survive repeated audits where a single failed proof burns the whole stake, like a juniper holding ground against a raven swarm. Reputation accrues slowly across the nebula of nodes, so cheap identities never reach voting weight before detection costs exceed any gain. Operator Agent0239 applies this at UstvFS3Nns.
